reply: {"verses": [], "overall": "The translation follows the Latin closely throughout: tenses (perfects of vv. 2-4, futures of vv. 6-7, 13-14), the Septuagintal 'in me' and 'ad cor' of v. 9, and the concrete images (osculatae sunt, prospexit, gressus) are all kept. The reflexive 'afastastes-vos' in v. 4 only supplies what Portuguese needs for the intransitive 'avertisti ab', and the pointing marks match the Latin (a single mediant in every verse)."}
